title: Elegoo Saturn 4 12K + ABS Like 3.0 Red Resin 1000g - $412.19 Delivered @ Elegoo Official AU Amazon AU
body:
Deal: Elegoo Saturn 4 12K + ABS Like 3.0 Red Resin 1000g - $412.19 Delivered @ Elegoo Official AU Amazon AU

[3dprintdeals] Great printer but you better know what you're up for if buying a resin printer.
A lot more safety precautions and space required.
[charmandad] It requires a lot of isopropyl alcohol to wash the model after printing, doesn't it? Would the cleaning cost end up being very high?
[3dprintdeals] Yes, but you can use the same batch of IPA for a while.
[tanabe88gg] don't worry about the cost of IPA, worry about the cost of setting up a safe area to keep the thing so you don't poison yourself and your family
[gfyc] I’ve never 3d printed before, would this one be good for a beginner? My son has gotten into miniature painting, we haven’t got many as they’re so expensive. A guy at the hobby shop said to get a resin printer for miniatures, make them yourself and this deal popped up. Thanks for any advice.
[3dprintdeals] for miniatures you'll want resin for the small size and high detail, just watch a few videos so you're prepared up front.
working space
clean & wash station
waste management
[gfyc] Thank you, I’m actually just starting to look into the setup now. The mars 5 ultra looked decent as it seemed easier for a newbie.
[3dprintdeals] watch a few videos from Once in a Six Side & Fauxhammer
You can get some decent results with FDM printers too now, even with stock 0.4mm nozzle but not as detailed as SLA
[gfyc] @3dprintdeals: Those abbreviations are still over my head but thank you. I’ll look it up and learn. AI is telling me we’d need a wash and curing station too. It also has said the mars 5 ultra is the go as it’s faster and is easier to use. For the small characters my son is painting I’ll be ok. Do you have any input as what to buy please?
[3dprintdeals] @gfyc: Saturn is the next step up in build plate size, but for miniatures, Mars is plenty. Many just fill up the build plate since it doesn't affect the print time.
FDM = filament printers like Bambu Lab
SLA = resin printers like this Elegoo Saturn
Mars 5 Ultra is plenty, and definitely get a wash & cure station as uncured resin is toxic.
You'll need part of your budget for plenty of IPA, gloves, PPE, paper towels and other bits & pieces but if he'll then have an endless supply of miniatures to paint. And, he may already have some PPE from painting if he's using airgun etc.
[Intoxicoligist] @gfyc: Hi!
The guy at the store is spot on, but in this case the Mars 5 (non ultra) is the same price as the Saturn 4 12K (non ultra), and the Saturn will allow your son to print larger models than the Mars. I started with a mars size printer and upgraded because I wanted the extra space (same use case, printing miniatures). In this case you're getting a bigger system for the current going price of a new mars 4 (although you might be able to find a better deal, I'm going off amazon pricing)
In terms of beginner friendly - it is as beginner friendly as resin printing can get, which is not very friendly at all! The uncured resin (think printer ink) is nasty and can cause an allergic reaction. Even the fumes from it are toxic (although they are ok to be vented to the atmosphere out a window). Plus the toxins build up in your system over time with prolonged exposure. It's definitely something that deserves respect, and its own dedicated space and procedures.
In terms of what you want to make, this printer at this price is better than the equivalent mars 5 at the same price. The Mars 5 technically has a better "resolution" on paper (finer print detail) but in reality most people use "anti aliasing" (very slightly blurs the prints to avoid voxel lines in your print) which makes it meaningless, plus I can't make out the difference in detail.
Budget a few hundred extra for supplies - resin, nitrile (not latex!) gloves, paper towel, cleaning solution (I use 99% isoproply alcohol, others use metho, and some resins can be washed in water, but they are advanced use cases), and a mask.
Let me know if you have any questions, but in general you can check out youtube for a quick guide on how to get set up, and what the dangers and common ways to avoid them are.
[Intoxicoligist] Will come down to how old your kid is (if you want them to print things themselves due to the toxic nature of resin) or if you're interested in getting into 3D printing as a hobby (it really is one in and of itself).
Most beginners start with a filament printer (rolls of plastic) which is safer, and easier for beginners, but also doesn't usually print with the same details as a resin printer. For terrain, the filament printers are usually great. But for anything smaller you'll probably want to look into resin, which can produce results similar or better than your local workshop of games
[ocdgamer] Dangit. I just purchased the Saturn 3 for $392 a couple weeks back.
This is a great deal
